newsitem.title: USA: U.S. hails treaty between Romania and Hungary.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hails treaty between Romania and Hungary.

text.p: The United States congratulated Romania and Hungary for their political courage in signing a treaty on Monday ending a centuries-old rift between the two neighbours.

The deal signed in Timisoara, Romania, caps five years of negotiations over the status of Romania's 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians and Bucharest's insistence that the pact should guarantee its borders.
"The U.S. government views this agreement as a significant achievement," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

Not only would the treaty strengthen relations between the two countries, "it will also demonstrate the commitment of Hungary and Romania to rejoin the Western community of democratic nations and is consistent with the purposes of NATO enlargement," he said.
The pact, agreed under Western pressure, is vital for both countries' ambitions to join the European Union and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
"The U.S. government congratulates both sides for the statesmanship and political courage they demonstrated in reaching this agreement," Burns said in a statement.
"We recognise that this treaty can make a valuable contribution to peace and stability in Central Europe and hope that it can be ratified and enter into effect soon."
